AdPilot

An agentic campaign optimization copilot that investigates advertising performance, surfaces a few defensible opportunities, and prepares changes that only an advertiser can approve.

Technical projectDecision & learning journalSee evidence

Demo status: The Streamlit prototype runs locally and is not yet publicly deployed. All campaigns, metrics, and approved changes are synthetic. This is not connected to Reddit, Microsoft, or any advertiser.

The customer problem

Performance marketers spend time moving between campaign dashboards to diagnose acquisition-cost changes, assess optimization opportunities, and apply updates. More alerts are not the answer. A useful assistant should reduce time to an appropriate action without distracting advertisers with weak recommendations or taking control away.

Fewer, better suggestions

At most three high-quality recommendations in a digest; zero is acceptable when evidence is weak.

Show the evidence

Explain observed CPA, delivery, reporting maturity and where marginal economics remain unknown.

Advertiser retains control

Preview budget effects, require explicit human approval, then verify simulated execution.

What each version has achieved

P0 · Functioning prototype (verified locally)
  • Integrated a real hosted Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite model with the OpenAI Agents SDK and Python advertising tools.
  • Observed an eight-tool campaign investigation in Terminal, including performance analysis, reporting checks, eligibility evaluation and a budget preview.
  • Delivered a Streamlit browser workflow with six synthetic campaigns, conversational investigation, a human approval step and sandbox action audit.
  • Confirmed updated daily budgets from $500 → $450 and $300 → $350, preserving the $800 combined daily budget. One sandbox action was recorded.

This demonstrates a working tool-calling workflow, not validated recommendation quality or production scale.

P0.5 · Agent quality and efficiency (underway)
  • The first live account-prioritization probe passed 9/10 process checks but skipped an explicit donor conversion-maturity read. A workflow validation fix was installed; 22/22 local unit tests passed, and a later trace checked both sides.
  • We challenged a misleading “must choose EU” heuristic check. Regrading the saved US selection with a revised process rubric gave 10/10 checks, but the independent US-versus-EU decision-quality review remained pending: the answer did not adequately compare both options.
  • Adding a stronger comparison instruction exposed orchestration costs: one run exceeded 15 agent turns; another hit Gemini's 15-requests/minute quota. These are runtime constraints, not proven recommendation inaccuracies.
  • A consolidated six-campaign snapshot tool has been prepared and offline-tested. Its real Gemini request savings and recommendation quality still need live verification.

Still unproven: higher expert-rated recommendation precision, real advertiser value, measured model-request savings or conversion lift. We track these separately from successful process and policy tests.

Why P0.5 changed the P1 architecture

Deliberate P0 choice: Start with six synthetic campaigns and straightforward per-campaign tools to prove that a hosted LLM can investigate, propose a bounded optimization, and preserve human approval. Bulk retrieval for thousands of campaigns would have added complexity before the core workflow was verified.

P0 · Prove the workflow

Validate genuine tool calls, campaign evidence, a non-executing proposal, and an auditable sandbox approval. The goal was functionality, not production scale or measured CPA improvement.

P0.5 · Discover the constraint

A fuller six-campaign evaluation recorded 17 tool calls. Explicit US/EU comparison then encountered a 15-turn ceiling and a separate Gemini 15-RPM limit. Investigation completeness and back-and-forth model orchestration became measurable product concerns.

P1 · Proposed design, not built

Fetch campaigns in backend batches, screen eligibility in conventional code, give Gemini a small evidence-rich shortlist, and allow focused follow-up lookups. Preserve independent safeguards and advertiser approval.

Proposed flow for larger advertisers

Bulk/paginated retrieval→Code-based eligibility screening→Evidence shortlist→Gemini comparison + optional deep dive→Guardrails + approval

The trade-off

We avoid sending every campaign's raw metrics to the model, reducing potential context and model-turn costs. But a strict prefilter could hide the best opportunity before Gemini sees it. Lower AI cost is not a win if decision quality or opportunity coverage declines.

What P1 evaluation must prove

Measure valuable-opportunity recall through the deterministic filter, supported top-3 recommendations, false abstention, safety, model calls/tokens, time-to-review and estimated cost across varied advertiser sizes. Compare against frozen cases and held-out examples, then validate in real-account shadow mode before any bounded pilot.

Status: This is an evaluation-informed architecture roadmap, not a claim that a 1,000-campaign backend has been built. The P0.5 account-snapshot patch is prepared and tested offline; its live improvement remains to be demonstrated. Read the detailed evidence and evaluation plan.

What I learned—and what I'm changing

1. Agents and deterministic checks have different jobs

The LLM chooses investigative tools and explains trade-offs. Deterministic functions calculate metrics, validate constraints and enforce write permissions. The model itself has no direct campaign execution tool.

2. Cloud inference without buying OpenAI API credits

Kept the OpenAI Agents SDK while connecting to the Gemini hosted API via its compatible endpoint. Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite worked after diagnosing unavailable models, timeouts and a malformed tool call. The key was created without enabling paid billing; free allowance and quotas must be verified before public hosting.

3. A successful demo is not a quality evaluation

One correctly executed synthetic transfer demonstrates wiring and approvals. It does not show that the recommendation was the best option or that performance would improve.

4. Failure traces are a roadmap

The next iteration will require broader candidate screening, maturity checks for both campaigns, clearer abstention criteria, and regression comparisons on frozen prompts. The goal is fewer false-positive suggestions, not more output.

Next release gate

Install the prepared six-campaign snapshot optimization and run the same frozen account-prioritization task. Compare complete versus partial investigations, model interaction count, process safeguards, and independently reviewed US/EU comparative reasoning. Rerun abstention and approval-boundary cases before claiming P0.5 progress. Production-scale P1 screening and any secured public demo remain future work; no measured advertiser time savings or CPA lift is claimed.
